proposal: The Mandate recommends that Congress wind down the Title VI international and area studies programs at universities, which it says sometimes fund programs counter to American interests. In the meantime it recommends a new regulation requiring the Secretary to allocate at least 40 percent of funding to international business programs that teach free markets and economics, and to require institutions, faculty and fellowship recipients to certify that they intend to serve American interests.

status_summary: Executive action has halted the current Title VI grants while Congress has kept the program funded. In 2025 ED issued non-continuation notices ending the Title VI international education grants, stating they were inconsistent with administration priorities, and moved about $86 million in combined FY2025 funds to a one-time investment in HBCUs; it also withdrew the FY2025 Fulbright-Hays application on 2025-05-09. On 2025-11-18 ED announced an international education and foreign language studies partnership with the State Department, which trade press reported covers 12 programs including the Title VI programs and four Fulbright-Hays programs. Congress provided $70.4 million for Title VI and $10.3 million for Fulbright-Hays in the FY2026 appropriations law signed 2026-02-03, and the FY2027 request again proposes eliminating the program. No statute winding down Title VI and no rule setting a 40 percent international business share or a certification requirement was found, so the stage reflects executive steps toward the outcome the text seeks, not the legislative wind-down or the interim rule it recommends.

timeline.event: A professional association noted ED's announcement of 2025-03-11 to cut its workforce by nearly half and said the office running Title VI and Fulbright-Hays might be eliminated, with no formal closure announced.
ED withdrew the FY2025 Fulbright-Hays application, according to a NAFSA tracker.

NAICU reported that ED ended Title VI international education grants through non-continuation notices, citing inconsistency with administration priorities, and reallocated about $86 million of FY2025 funds to HBCUs.

timeline.event: The University of Michigan International Institute reported that its six Title VI National Resource Centers operated until 2025-09-10 and listed its NRC and FLAS programs as canceled after federal funding changes.

ED announced an International Education and Foreign Language Studies Partnership with the State Department covering programs administered under Fulbright-Hays (the ED page shows a last-reviewed date of 2025-11-18).

The PIE News reported that 12 programs move to the State Department under the agreement, including Title VI programs (National Resource Centers, FLAS fellowships, Centers for International Business Education and others) and four Fulbright-Hays programs.
The President signed the consolidated FY2026 appropriations act, which provides $70.4 million for Title VI and $10.3 million for Fulbright-Hays at ED, per NAFSA.
The FY2027 budget request proposed eliminating the Title VI International Education program, described as currently funded at $81 million, per a university federal relations summary.

uncertainties: The NAICU and NAFSA pages are association trackers without printed dates (the NAICU date is taken from its URL). The ED release on the State partnership names only Fulbright-Hays; the inclusion of Title VI programs and the count of 12 programs come from The PIE News. NAFSA gives no House figure for Title VI, while The PIE News and NAICU say the House FY2026 bill provided nothing. The University of Michigan page has no exact date (it is labeled as of October 2025; 2025-10-01 is used as an approximation). The $81 million in the FY2027 summary appears to be the combined Title VI and Fulbright-Hays line (NAFSA gives $80.7 million combined), which is an inference. Whether ED or State has run new Title VI competitions with FY2026 funds was not found: an ED FLAS program page still lists an FY2026 competition and gives no transfer notice. The closure of the International and Foreign Language Education office was not confirmed. No 40 percent rule or certification requirement was found.
